segments.text: KTD, gold cold against my chest.
My father gave me more than metal.
He gave me what was left.
An intermediary took the light, a shadow on the floor.
Displaying lineage on a stage that didn't know the law.
The pride was loud, the room was bright, the steel was in their hand.
But shadows don't belong to crowds, they belong to the man.
You can steal the shine, but you cannot own what the memory means.
KTD still standing within these tragic scenes.
The chain came home, but the night got colder.
Gold on my skin, weight on my shoulder.
Weight on my shoulder.
The recovery was quiet, no cameras in the rain.
A price for every heartbeat, a tax for every grain.
The latest strike was heavy.
I felt the bone give in.
Shoulder and the arm injured beneath the heavy skin.
I survived the consequence, I didn't seek the praise.
Just walking through the fog of these dark and heavy days.
A wound is not a chorus.
A scar is not a crown.
Scar is not a crown.
I don't turn a man's ending into a trophy I can hold down.
KTD respects the earth, I respect the things that grow.
The wind don't need a witness for the way the leaves blow.
You can steal the shine, but you cannot own what the memory means.
KTD still standing within these tragic scenes.
The chain came home, but the night got colder.
Gold on my skin, weight on my shoulder.
Weight on my shoulder.
The tree did not chase him.
It simply stayed where trees do.
I keep my father's chain, my arm, my shoulder, my breath.
